> If someone doubts the reality of the threat, go and check out

> agree with TK that _all_ technology is inherently evil. It's

I recently read an article that said "WE are the comet". It spoke of how
1 in 5 species would soon become extinct because of humans' impact on
the earth. it said that "suppose there were a threat of a comet in 30
years... would we do anything, or would the corporates not want anyone
to know because it might rock the boat & cause job loss, etc.". The
article said "well, our impact on the planet is likely to be as severe
as that of a comet, and we're talking a 30 year time frame here, 30
years to change before it's too late."

I'd also like to add something I wanted to say awhile ago. There was a
discussion about the morality of the manifesto. People were talking
about what was more important, human suffering or human freedom? I meant
to jump in with one fact: the manifesto argues that technology's impact
on the planet and on the human race was IRREVERSIBLE. The planet's life
support would be so altered that it would be impossible to ever go back
& live without technology, humans would become like a geriatric patient
on oxygen, and once they started tinkering with human genetics, the
natural human being would be a thing of the past, replaced by something
manufactured.
Under such conditions, what would be the point of living?

Given such a future, I totally understand the manifesto's extreme
conclusion that it would be better to "dump the whole stinking system". 

After all, during the Cold War our generals believed "better dead than
red". They believed that the Communist system exerted such tyranny over
people that even thinking about freedom would be impossible (a phrase
echoed in the manifesto in regards to behavior control). Therefore they
believed that it would be preferable to launch the nukes & condemn
everyone to living a radioactive half-life, if you catch my pun.

The manifesto is extremely persuasive in arguing this theme. It's no
wonder the feds didn't want Ted's political views aired during the
trial.
